Tenant and node network lifecycle: Build Kubernetes-native automation to create, modify, and remove tenant networks and manage node membership through provisioning, scaling, repair, replacement, and reassignment. Verify isolation and connectivity at each transition, recover safely from partial failures, and remove stale configuration before resources are reassigned. Data center routing and connectivity: Own dynamic configuration of tenant networks, BGP, routing policy, VLANs, and overlays across management, tenant, and external networks. Build Kubernetes-native automation to provision and manage these capabilities through fabric-manager APIs, including customer service exposure, ingress/egress, VIPs, load balancers, and public IPs. GPU networking: Automate tenant configuration and lifecycle operations for GPU networking, including NVL72 systems, InfiniBand, RoCE, and GPUDirect, through supported platform and fabric-management interfaces. Addressing and fabric integration: Own dynamic address allocation, network inventory integration, and tenant network configuration through IPAM, NetBox, and fabric-manager APIs such as Netris and UFM. Keep intended configuration, applied state, and inventory consistent throughout the tenant and node lifecycle. Tenant isolation and network security: Own segmentation and traffic policy across the Groq management plane, tenant clusters, and physical fabrics. Define permitted communication between environments and verify isolation through provisioning, scaling, maintenance, and hardware reassignment. Work with security engineering on network access controls and hardening requirements. Network standards and configuration lifecycle: Establish addressing, routing, and configuration standards for GroqMetal’s management plane and tenant networks. Detect and reconcile configuration drift, and maintain tenant isolation as nodes enter, leave, or return to tenant networks during provisioning, repair, and reassignment. Production network reliability: Own network telemetry, troubleshooting, and incident remediation. Diagnose packet loss, routing failures, congestion, and unexpected traffic across hosts, clusters, fabrics, and the edge. Turn recurring incidents and performance findings into prioritized improvements to the managed service. You understand TCP/IP, BGP, routing policy, peering, ECMP, segmentation, and interconnects well enough to explain packet paths, diagnose failures, and evaluate the consequences of a configuration change. Bare-metal data center networking expertise: Experience operating leaf-spine fabrics, underlay and overlay networks, and tenant separation using technologies such as VLANs, VRFs, and EVPN/VXLAN. Strong Kubernetes and Linux networking experience: Practical knowledge of CNI behavior, Cilium or comparable systems, network policy, service exposure, and the interaction between cluster networking and physical infrastructure. You can integrate network APIs through reconciliation loops that handle retries, partial failures, and resource cleanup safely. You have managed changes through version control, code review, automated testing, and controlled rollout. Experience building multitenant infrastructure or managed Kubernetes products: You have helped deliver Kubernetes networking as a service, including customer onboarding, provisioning, upgrades, scaling, and production support. You can turn customer requirements into supported features with defined behavior, limits, and operational procedures. Experience securing networks that run customer workloads: You have designed and operated tenant separation, management network boundaries, and traffic controls, with practical methods for testing that those controls work. Fabric management and IPAM experience: Netris, UFM, NetBox, or comparable fabric management and IPAM systems. GPU infrastructure expertise: NVIDIA GPU infrastructure and AI networking, including InfiniBand, Spectrum-X, NVL72 systems, RDMA, RoCE, and congestion control. GPU cluster networking experience: Networking for large GPU clusters, including distributed workload performance, high-bandwidth east-west traffic, and multi-site connectivity. Excellence Is The Standard: High performance isn’t just encouraged, it’s the baseline. And it’s contagious. This range is specific to candidates located in the United States. Compensation for international candidates will vary based on local market dynamics. Beyond cash compensation, Groq also offers a Long-Term Incentive (LTI) Program and a robust suite of employee benefits.
